summary: Reader v2 for kernel-log dumps that lost their KL begin record is written and tested on the host. kl_reader2.py derives the dump geometry (len, head, tail, gap) from the KL end line (recs, bytes) and the received offsets (below the cap len = bytes; at the cap len = the end of the last tail record, which must have the final 32-byte size or the group is refused), verifies it (end-line counts, the 96-byte grid, the image's send order, no repeated offset), and feeds accepted groups through NAT-089's own merge/holes/text; otherwise the group is listed under `unreadable` with the reason and no text is made of it. analyze_nat097.py applies NAT-089's row logic (A1-A8, imported unchanged) over that text and names an inferred dump in the result. On the real NAT-093 archive (a local artifact) it finds one inferred dump of length 170,097 (head 8,192, tail 32,768, gap 129,137), 345 of 428 records, holes [137329,142129) and [145489,148657) = 7,968 bytes, equal to docs/procedures/nat-093/posthoc.json and to the bytes the hand reader read; the row on that archive stays A8 (no launchd line in the surviving text), so the new reader changes how the text is obtained and not what NAT-093 showed. Dumps with a real begin are read exactly as NAT-089's reader reads them (tests compare the two). 50 tests pass; mutation: 223 killed, 7 survivors (examined, equivalent), 15 invalid candidates, after a first pass that left 22 survivors of which 15 showed missing assertions (tests added, pass repeated). Nothing here measures the phone.

acceptance.1_real_archive: RealNat093 tests (skipped when the local archive is absent; none skipped): one dump, begin_inferred true, len 170097, head 8192, tail 32768, gap 129137, 345 records, 7968 hole bytes, holes equal to posthoc.json's missing list and to [[137329,142129],[145489,148657]], bytes equal to what posthoc_boot2.read_boot returns, no conflicts, extra offsets or problems; the analyser's row on that archive is A8 'no launchd line in the returned text' while NAT-089's reader says A8 'no why=2 dump with text'. findings: The real NAT-093 archive's missing records include the begin line and the first tail record (offset 137329): the producer's ring overrun took the start of the dump, which is where the begin is.

Tests were added (44 -> 50) and the pass repeated (artifacts/nat-097/mutation-2): 0 unexplained survivors. Code was not changed between the passes.

results.reason: `line` of a group is only the sort key that puts the inferred dumps of one boot in order with its real dumps (the sort is by the index of a dump's first line). Every stray line of a group lies after the previous dump's last line and before the next dump's `begin`, because the producer sends dumps one after another and a begin or an end line closes or opens a dump in parse_kl; so the index of the group's first line and the index of its last line fall in the same gap between neighbours and give the same order. The two differ only if a complete dump with its own begin sat inside one group, which the sender cannot produce.
